# Airlocks Airlocks are used to control access to different areas of the station.
Airlocks can be opened using either [color=yellow][bold][keybind="Use"][/bold][/color] with an empty hand, [color=yellow][bold][keybind="ActivateItemInWorld"][/bold][/color] if hands are full, or by colliding with the airlock.
Airlocks will only open if you have an ID card with the correct access level. The ID card must be in your hand, an ID slot, or a PDA in one of those two locations. If you have multiple IDs, the airlock will check them all when you try to open it.
Airlocks block gas flow, so they can be used to seal off areas in case of a [textlink="hull breach" link="Spacing"] or a [textlink="fire." link="Fires"] They also store gas on their tile, even when closed, so be careful when opening them during or after a gas leak.
## Bolting Airlocks can be bolted to prevent them from being opened or pried open by hand. When this occurs, the airlock will display red lights on the top of the door.
## Emergency Access
The [bold]emergency access terminal[/bold] is a unique computer located inside the bridge that is able to remotely toggle emergency access on airlocks. This is done by inputting an airlock's emergency access code (found by examining the airlock at close range) into the terminal.
When an airlock is in emergency access mode, it'll display yellow blinking lights and will allow any person to pass, regardless of their ID access.
## Styling Airlocks can come in different styles to match station departments. The department style commonly reflects the required access level. They can also be repainted with a spray painter.
## Wiring Airlocks have internal wiring, which can be opened using a screwdriver. Each wire controls some aspect of the airlock's functionality, depending on which wires are cut, mended, or pulsed.
To see a full list of wires and what they do, refer to the [textlink="wires" link="Wires"] page.
